_comment: Hand-validated wait times for well-known interchanges. Used by `--validate` (check 6) to catch regressions. Tolerance: ±1 minute. Update when TfL frequencies change.
_model: Wait = COMBINED frequency of every line sharing a boarding hop (see combine_shared_hops). On shared track a rider boards whichever train comes first, so all lines on a hop share one wait; a line's own headway only shows once it splits onto its own branch.
_kings_cross: Kings Cross is the densest interchange. The sub-surface hop to Euston Sq is Circle+H&C+Metropolitan combined, so all three read the same low wait.
_central_core: 27-34 tph on core White City to Leytonstone.
_circle_hc: Sub-surface core: Circle+H&C+Metropolitan interleave on the same track, so the combined frequency is high and the shared hop reads a 1-min wait. Edgware Rd is a Circle/District pivot with fewer trains combining, so it stays a touch higher.
_district_trunk: Trunk through central London ~8-10 tph combined.
_metropolitan_trunk: Metropolitan uses its OWN platforms at Baker St (Circle/H&C share a different platform), so Met does not combine with them. Its 4 branches combine among themselves to a ~2-min trunk wait.
_overground_shared: Overground lines only combine where TfL platform data confirms a shared platform. Lioness/Bakerloo at Harrow board separate platforms; Canonbury exposes no platform data, so Mildmay/Windrush do NOT combine there and each keeps its own ~3-min wait.
_overground_high_freq: Windrush core (combined sub-branches) is more frequent.
_elizabeth_core: 16 tph core; ~3-min headway floors to a 1-min wait.
_branch_endings: Outer branches lower freq. Same-platform shares still combine (Uxbridge-Hillingdon: Metropolitan+Piccadilly board the same platform). But Elizabeth and Piccadilly serve Heathrow on separate stations/platforms, so the Piccadilly wait to T2&3 stays its own single-line value.
